title: Order of Charging and Funding Tally
note: The statutory Order of Charging and the sibling-slice tally. What a request still needs is the hospital bill less PhilHealth coverage less any other coverage already applied, and only that residual is ever endorsed. computeFunding then separates money an agency has approved from money still in flight, which is what stops CRMC endorsing past the remaining balance.
trimmed: the deriveAmountNeeded legacy wrapper and the one-line isCommittedSlice helper.

title: Request Status Derivation and the Slice-Terminal Test
note: A request’s lifecycle state is derived from its money rather than stored beside it, so the status a patient reads can never disagree with the figures underneath. isSliceTerminal decides when one agency’s slice is finished, which is what separates the patient’s in-progress list from their history.
trimmed: deriveRequestFinancials, which re-derives a parent request from its slices during a reversal, and the explanatory comments.

title: CRMC Endorsement Transaction
note: Endorsement is where one request becomes several funding slices. Every read happens before every write, as Firestore’s transaction contract requires, and the whole thing commits or fails together: either every selected agency receives a slice and loses a daily slot, or none does.
trimmed: the patient-detail fields copied onto each slice, the watcher list, and the post-transaction document stamping.

title: Agency Approval and Budget Commitment
note: The approval transaction closes the race in which two coordinators approving at the same moment could each pass a client-side budget check and together overspend the allocation. The agency record is re-read inside the transaction, and the parent request’s secured total advances in the same commit.
trimmed: the Hospital ID cooldown stamp, several recorded fields on the slice, and the comment blocks explaining each one.

title: Representative Firestore Security Rules
note: Authorization lives in the rules, not in the interface, on the principle that the interface is a convenience and the rules are the boundary. Four guards are representative: a user cannot raise their own role, an agency cannot approve more than CRMC endorsed, an audit entry is bound to the account that wrote it and can never be altered, and an agency cannot issue a Guarantee Letter against another agency’s application.
trimmed: the helper definitions (isAuth, isAdmin, isAgency, userAgencyId) and the read rules, which are longer and less instructive than the write guards.

title: Selfie Retention Cloud Function
note: Compliance with Republic Act No. 10173 is implemented as behaviour rather than asserted in a policy document. When a request reaches a terminal state the live-selfie image is deleted, while the metadata and the non-biometric verdict flags are kept for audit and the identity document, which is the proof of record, is left intact.
trimmed: the Cloud Function wrapper binding the handler to the requests/{requestId} write trigger, and the error logging.
